# General Research Superpowers: framework plan

## Purpose
A domain-neutral research framework for any thesis topic, scientific study or evidence-based investigation. It does not assume a personal project, dataset, industry, target variable or model architecture. The framework supplies procedures; the host supplies tools and execution. It is not a trained foundation model or a deployed autonomous service.

## Architecture
1. Frame the question, scope and contribution.
2. Select a suitable study type: descriptive, exploratory, predictive, causal, theoretical, qualitative or mixed-methods.
3. Establish source/data provenance and an appropriate evidence contract.
4. Load relevant methods and execute within the authorized resource budget.
5. Challenge findings with design-appropriate checks and document uncertainty/limitations.
6. Reproduce computational results where applicable and write traceable reports, theses or papers.

The specialist catalog is strongest in quantitative and computational research. General framing/reporting supports other approaches, but detailed qualitative, historical and formal-proof workflows require additional disciplinary guidance. Do not force every question into machine learning or null-hypothesis testing.

## Method portfolio
The 28 skills cover framing, preregistration, provenance, null models, critical review, evidence tracking, reporting, routing, EDA, pattern mining, classical ML, AutoML, experimentation, causal inference, time series, uncertainty, reliability, physics-informed models, literature review, reproducibility and scientific writing.

## Scientific controls
- Distinguish exploration from confirmation and preserve prior outcome exposure.
- Use inference/evaluation units appropriate to the design.
- Protect evaluation outcomes and keep transformations inside training folds.
- Identify causal effects before estimation; state assumptions and sensitivity.
- Match null generation to dependence and exchangeability.
- Account for model/parameter selection and multiple comparisons.
- Treat source provenance as separate from evidential validity.
- Use evidence criteria appropriate to quantitative, qualitative or theoretical claims.
- Record consequential choices and proceed on authorized reversible work.

## External references
Use the source register for scientific libraries and reusable skill candidates. Selectively inspect, pin and test any adopted component; no full external collection is required. Some candidate skill bodies remain unreviewed because retrieval was incomplete. No external skill was bulk-installed.

## Roadmap
| Stage | Status / acceptance |
|---|---|
| General methods and routing | Implemented: 28 indexed skills |
| Structural and helper validation | Run the validator and regression suite |
| Host integration | Pending: verify skill discovery and relevant loading |
| Study pilot | Pending: choose a representative authorized dataset or source collection |
| Comparative evaluation | Pending: compare original/upgraded behavior on matched held-out tasks and budgets |
| Specialist extensions | Add only when a study needs a method not adequately covered |

Evaluate routing, question alignment, design validity, source fidelity, leakage prevention, uncertainty, reproducibility, usefulness and resource adherence. Fabricated evidence and invalid inference are critical failures regardless of writing quality. Preserve task traces and distinguish static checks from empirical evidence of agent improvement.

## First use
Select one research question and a small representative evidence sample. Establish a valid protocol and baseline/argument, produce one traceable result, and verify the process before scaling the study. See [general workflows](research-workflows.md) and the [source register](sources.md).

## Added review and communication layer

Six skills now cover explicit problem statements, self-review, peer review rounds, tutor review, outsider review and executive summaries. See [workflow and boundaries](review-and-communication-workflow.md). Native coordination remains a separate proposed implementation.
